key_insight: Fine-tuned LLMs can generate synthetic dyslipidemia data that closely preserve real-world clinical patterns for exploratory cardiovascular research.
clinical_relevance: Synthetic datasets may help researchers analyze secondary prevention and build models when access to patient-level data is limited by privacy or logistics.
method: Two real-world Centro Cardiologico Monzino datasets on dyslipidemia/secondary cardiovascular prevention were used.
Pre-trained LLMs were fine-tuned inside secure infrastructure to synthesize tabular clinical records.
Synthetic data were compared with original and anonymized data using fidelity, privacy, and clinical utility metrics.
evidence_signal: Synthetic data showed strong agreement with source data, with meaningful distributional differences limited to a few variables and key predictor-outcome relationships largely preserved.
watch_item: Some effect sizes were slightly attenuated, so synthetic data should be validated before use in confirmatory analyses or high-stakes decisions.
paper_title: Evaluation of AI-Generated Synthetic Data for Clinical Research in Secondary Cardiovascular Prevention among Dyslipidemia Patients
